gpt.text:
Run the three “Next Commands” in order, and after each one, capture the key outputs so we can decide what (if anything) to promote to champion.

## 1) AUB autopilot (module-level selection)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
What to look for / paste back:
- Which module candidate (if any) was selected as “best”
- The evaluation summary table (means/mins, deltas vs champion)
- Any failures/timeouts

If it selects a best candidate, note the candidate file path/hash and whether it changes `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json` or produces a new artifact.

## 2) System autopilot (system-level candidates)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
What to look for / paste back:
- The ranked results for each system candidate
- Any candidate that beats champion on the primary metric(s) (you listed tuning_mean/min and lockbox_mean/min—confirm which is the gate)
- Any “regressions” flags or constraint violations

## 3) Next-fix report generation
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
What to look for / paste back:
- The top recommended fixes and their rationale
- Any referenced failing tests/benchmarks and the suggested patch locations

## Quick sanity checks before/if something looks off
- Confirm the champion file exists and is readable:
  ```bash
  ls -l baseline/champion_v5_latest.json
  ```
- If runs are nondeterministic, re-run the winning candidate once to confirm it holds.

If you paste the stdout summaries (or the generated report files/paths), I can tell you whether anything should be promoted and what the next iteration should target.
